fit_table.src: carbon rod in a resin socket: the 3.2 / 6.2 bores for 3 / 6 rods (CLAUDE.md), the resin fills the rest: it only has to go in (Overseer coupons v2, Spark 27 Oct: the largest of the coupon bores fit; OD + 0.3 was loose in PETG)

a D bore pressed on the N20's 3.0 / 2.5 D shaft: drawn 3.3 / 2.8 (+0.3 on the diameter and across the flat) pushes on by hand, a drop of CA (the probe coupon, Spark 14 Nov: D1 3.0 / 2.5 and D2 3.1 / 2.6 would not go on, D3 3.2 / 2.7 too hard to press home; printed holes come out ~0.1-0.2 small). min_gap: the drawn clearance per side the check accepts, 0.15 less the viewing mesh's 0.05 (D3's 0.1 failed by hand at 0.10 drawn, so a press mate is checked against the shaft's own D, not a round stand-in)
a bore turning free on an M3 axle or a 3 mm rod: 3.3 (coupon A1, the snuggest of 3.3 / 3.4 / 3.5, all free)
a bought body sliding into a printed pocket, sleeve or slot over its length (camera case, SG90 body): the axle's +0.3 plus 0.3 for the long contact and the case's own tolerance; check on the bench
a printed part sliding onto another printed part: both faces print GROW fat (0.2 of it gone) + 0.3 running
parts that pass each other and must never touch (an assembly path past a neighbour, a moving part)
a screw's shank through a printed clearance hole: M2 2.4, M3 3.4
a screw cutting its own thread in a printed pilot: M2 1.6, M3 2.6 (the SG90 tab pilots)

a screw's shank close-fit through a printed hole where it locates the part (the Overseer arms' M3 3.2 as the rod bore, overseer_arm_lib HOLE_D / SLOT_D; the carbon plates' Ø3.1 / 3.0 M; the hub deck's M2 2.2)
the resin injection port for one 14 G blunt tip (OD 2.11): Ø2.5 (Spark 8 Nov, CLAUDE.md; cage_node_lib PORT_R)
a hex nut's pocket across its flats: M3 5.5 -> 5.7 (overseer_arm_lib NUT_AF; not recorded in dimensions.md)

pairs.contact: the head's cable coil is drawn as a solid ring over the drum's O8 hub (a loose coil, nothing printed in it)
the 40 / 12 gear mesh: the teeth are drawn at an arbitrary phase
the blades leave the wound coil at its tangent (the feed drawn from the coil's surface)
the horn's hub on the SG90's spline, 0.25 off the case on the spline's shoulder (the spline itself not drawn)

mates.why: the cradle turns between the head frame's brackets
the pinion's D bore on the N20's 3.0 / 2.5 D shaft
the spool turns between the bench turret's side plates
the N20's shaft in the tip bearing's 3.2 bore (the fit table's close fit, its tightest joint), its gearbox between the bench turret's rails (press, 0.15 a side) and on the face plate; no screws

paths.name: pinion up into its bay
paths.why: in hand, the turret off the base and upside down: the 12 T pinion (O11.42, its O7 hub boss toward the tip bearing) into its bay through the bay's open bottom (11.92 wide, 24 Nov: it had no way in); it waits there for the N20's shaft

paths.name: N20 in along +y between its rails
paths.why: the N20's gearbox and can (their 12 x 10 x 27 box) straight in along +y, under the -y wall's notched foot, the gearbox between the two rails 12.3 apart (the fit table's press: a hand push), onto the face plate; no screws (24 Nov: the 2 x M1.6 had no driver line past the tip bearing and their heads stood in the pinion): the rails take its torque, the plate, the pressed pinion and the base's opening hold it along y

paths.name: N20's shaft through the pinion into the tip bearing
paths.why: the N20's 3 mm D shaft through the face plate's O4.4 hole, pressed through the pinion's D bore (the pinion held against the tip bearing's block) and into the tip bearing's 3.2 bore: the pinion is pressed on in place, it cannot pass the plate's hole

paths.name: roller in from behind
paths.why: the pressure roller (rod, two tubes, saddle and leaf) in through the spool's bay from behind (-x), before the spool, then out along its radial guides, the saddle and leaf into their pocket (the rod in its 3.3 slots: the fit table's free fit)

paths.name: spool in from behind and above
paths.why: the spool with its gear, drum hub, cable coil and the blades' ends down and forward (+x, 0.6 down per mm) between the two side walls, its drum hub and coil along the drum's U (24 Nov: the ring was closed), its gear over the floor, onto the pinion and against the roller (it turns as the teeth meet; the gear mesh and the roller's leaf are its seats)

paths.name: spool axle M3 x 50 in from -y
paths.why: the spool's axle, an M3 x 50 screw (its head at the -y wall, the nyloc at the +y one), in from -y through both bosses and the spool's bore

paths.name: bench turret onto the bench base
paths.why: last of the kit: the bench turret with its pinion, N20, roller, spool (cable coil, blades) and axle in it, down onto the base (its floor bosses on the base's inserts, 4 x M3 x 8 from above); the N20 hangs in the base's opening, which leaves it 3.0 of the 9.85 its shaft needs, so it is in before this

paths.name: blades into the head frame's clip
paths.why: the two blades' tips (the lens, 2 x 2.78 thick, 19 wide) slide up into the head frame's 14 mm clip

paths.name: SG90 into the head frame's ring
paths.why: step 2 (parts/scout_v4_head_lib.py): the SG90 with its horn slid +y into the frame's closed ring from the cradle's room, its tabs stop on the ring's face

paths.name: camera into the cradle (in hand)
paths.why: step 3: the case slid into the cradle from behind until its front meets the lip, the cradle still off the head (Spark 15 Nov: it could not)

paths.name: cradle lowered onto the horn
paths.why: step 5: the cradle with the camera and LED bars at nod 0 lowered straight down between the bracket and the SG90, the horn's arm, hub and centre screw sliding up its channel from the open bottom edge; with the horn here (shown lifted out together; head_frame/make.py checks the channel over the horn)

paths.name: head nods -20..+90 deg
paths.why: the cradle, camera and LED bars about the SG90's axis from 20 down to 90 up (parked 15 up)
